correctness.rationale: Success is equivalent to at least three survivors with at least two represented specialist classes; when all three classes are represented no edge is needed, and when exactly two are represented one extra edge gives an injective three-plant matching. Subtraction of disjoint one-class survival events yields the exact formula. Two Pascal-identity steps give the strictly positive second forward difference p² q^(n-m-2)(1-q^m) for all admissible m, proving unique balancing by transfer; zero concentration penalty iff each class has size at most two gives the sharp n<=6 upper-bound cutoff. Standalone exhaustive matching assignment checker passed 252 exact rational identities and 252 allocation comparisons; finite results are corroboration, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: Three host plants, independent loss of specialist service units, unit match capacity and one contingent new interaction is a motivated, capacity-limited ecological restoration benchmark. The theorem gives an exact all-n and all-p optimal redundancy allocation, a strict improvement law for every imbalance, and a sharp n=6 boundary for attaining the physical survivor-count bound. Unlike a table or arbitrary slice, it has a canonical resource-allocation variable and explains the appearance of unavoidable one-guild concentration failures.
